geo.label: Fed lift-off intact into a war shock
parts: Macro Stance

Friday's violent relief rally has already been partly overtaken. The S&P 500 closed at 4,384.65 index points (+2.24% on the day, +0.10% over five sessions) and the Nasdaq 100 at 14,189.16 index points (+1.53%), while the VIX fell 2.73 points to 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters framed it as investors digesting sanctions on Russia [[n1223]], after Fortune described the week's reversal as one of the incredible vaults in equity-market history [[n0121]]. That rally priced the first sanctions package; The New York Times then reported the US and Europe will bar some Russian banks from SWIFT [[n1412]]. Mixed: US earnings are less exposed than Europe's, but multiples rest on a Fed that experts quoted by Business Insider say will not rescue a meltdown [[n0803]].
Rates & Curve

The curve says the Fed matters more than the war. The 2Y closed at 1.55% and the 10Y at 1.97%, leaving 10Y-2Y at +42 bps, with the 3M at 0.33% and 10Y-3M at +164 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25). Over 20 observations the 2Y rose 37 bps from 1.18% and the 10Y 16 bps from 1.81%, so the spread compressed by 21 bps: the curve is positively sloped and the 20-observation move is a bear flattening, both up with the 2Y up more. Over five observations the 2Y added 6 bps and the 10Y was unchanged, meaning the safe-haven bid Reuters described on invasion day [[n0208]] only anchored the long end. Xinhua reported a Fed official signalling a March hike remains on track despite Ukraine [[n2180]].
New / Most Important

First, the SWIFT step, which CBC said Canada is joining [[n1416]], moves sanctions from named lenders to the payment rails, raising settlement risk for anyone still clearing Russian flows. Second, demand was already softening: The Conference Board said consumer confidence declined for a second consecutive month in February [[n2087]], and Builder reported pending home sales falling for a third straight month in January [[n2110]], against the largest annual consumer-price gain in 40 years [[n2032]]. Corporate cash is going to buybacks, with CNBC reporting a record $27 billion Berkshire repurchase in 2021 [[n0806]]. The DXY slipped 0.54% to 96.62 index points on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) after Reuters had reported the dollar near a two-year high on invasion day [[n1210]].
Playbook ✓

Action: hold US quality large caps and energy over long-duration growth, and keep index hedges on while the VIX sits at 27.59 index points. Trigger to add risk: the S&P 500 holding Friday's 4,384.65 close as markets absorb the SWIFT measures, with the VIX failing to regain 30.49, its late-January level (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). What changes the call: a front end that keeps rising while the 10Y stalls would deepen the bear flattening from +42 bps and signal tightening into a growth shock; Reuters has already reported louder calls for 50 bps rather than 25 bps in March [[n2040]]. The State of the Union on March 1 [[n0118]] tests whether Washington pairs sanctions with energy-price relief.

geo.label: ECB taper meets energy shock
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is where the weekend's escalation lands hardest. Friday's bounce lifted the STOXX 600 3.32% to 453.53 index points and the DAX 3.67% to 14,567.23 index points, yet both remain down 2.58% and 4.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Since then Europe has moved to remove Russian banks from SWIFT, per Global Finance [[n1226]], and to shut its airspace to Russian airlines while funding weapons purchases for Ukraine, per PBS [[n1225]]. Bearish: the region carries the energy, banking and trade exposure that sanctions and counter-sanctions now target.
Activity & Inflation

The growth starting point was respectable, with Times of Malta reporting euro-zone growth jumping as virus restrictions eased [[n1144]]. The price side is the problem: Eurostat put energy inflation at 27% [[n1220]], and The Guardian argued the war will fuel a sharp further hike [[n1222]]. Dutch TTF gas closed at 94.42 EUR/MWh, down 29.70% on Friday but up 26.04% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), a volatility profile that makes industrial hedging expensive. ECB policymakers told Reuters not to go back on quicker taper plans [[n1224]], so the stagflation trade-off is live.
New / Most Important

Germany's U-turn is the regime change. DW reported a €100 billion commitment to defence spending [[n1228]], Reuters quoted Scholz calling it a response to 'Putin's war' [[n1229]], and Clean Energy Wire reported plans for strategic gas and coal reserves [[n1221]]. Fiscal expansion for security and energy storage is inflationary at the margin, supportive for defence and grid suppliers, and a direct cost to taxpayers.
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight euro-area banks with Russian subsidiaries and energy-intensive cyclicals; overweight defence. Societe Generale closed at 28.45 EUR, down 12.09% over five sessions, while Rheinmetall closed at 107.05 EUR, up 11.00% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: add to the bank underweight if TTF rebuilds Friday's 29.70% drop. What changes the call: a credible negotiation track that takes TTF back below 92.30 EUR/MWh, its late-January level, which would ease the margin squeeze on industry and the inflation pressure on the ECB.

geo.label: Easing bias, offshore discount
parts: Macro Stance

China is trading as a policy-insulated onshore market and a sanctions-sensitive offshore one. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,451.41 index points, up 0.63% on Friday and down only 1.13% over five sessions, while the Hang Seng closed at 22,767.18 index points, down 6.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Beijing's line, which PBS described as avoiding criticism of the Russian attack while calling for talks [[n1350]], keeps it outside the Western coalition; The New York Times reported US officials had repeatedly urged China to help avert the war [[n1395]]. Mixed: onshore policy support is real, but the offshore market is pricing regulatory and geopolitical risk at the same time.
PMIs & Activity

The last private factory gauge was weak: Reuters reported January Caixin activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit [[n0139]]. Against that, China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved [[n0137]], and Best Selling Cars Blog put January vehicle wholesales up 0.9% in a stable market [[n0162]]. Structural drags show up regionally, with SCMP reporting a rust-belt province unveiling a population plan in the face of economic decline [[n0185]]. Power investment is the bright spot: Global Times reported an expected record 75-90GW of solar additions [[n0181]]. The February PMIs are the next activity test; until then the read is soft manufacturing and policy-led investment.
Credit Impulse

The policy direction is easier even before the credit numbers confirm it. Reuters reported that slowing inflation leaves room for policy easing [[n0149]], and Bloomberg described the People's Bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0134]]. That divergence is the core of the China call: the US 2Y has risen 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25) while Beijing leans the other way. The constraint is transmission through a stressed property sector and a tighter grip on platform finance; The Japan Times reported regulators telling banks and state firms to report exposure to Jack Ma's Ant [[n0161]]. Easing channelled through state lenders and infrastructure should lift onshore equities before it lifts household consumption.
Property

Property is still triage rather than recovery. Reuters reported Evergrande selling four projects to state-owned firms for $337 mln [[n0220]], and SCMP described Chinese firms picking away at its assets [[n0228]]. CNBC reported Moody's downgrading Shimao as debt troubles drag on [[n0205]], and The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over its bond default [[n0170]]. The pattern is a controlled transfer of viable projects into state hands, which limits systemic contagion but leaves private developers' offshore bondholders at the back of the queue. For equities, it means the property drag on steel, building materials and household wealth persists even as policy eases at the margin.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The next policy signal is the annual 'two sessions', which SCMP previewed as Beijing plotting its course [[n0212]]; the growth target and fiscal quota will set the tone for the quarter. Hong Kong is already spending, with Al Jazeera reporting a $22bn budget as zero-COVID hammers businesses [[n0187]]. Trade cuts both ways. Reuters reported Russia's trade flows shifting towards China as sanctions start [[n1281]], and Global Times quoted analysts saying the agricultural-trade impact on China is limited [[n0209]]. Doubts over the phase-one deal, which SCMP asked was a 'historic failure' [[n0233]], and the Peterson Institute's finding that China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports [[n0145]] make secondary measures a tail risk if Beijing is seen to cushion Moscow.
Markets & Flows

Offshore internet is where the discount is applied. Tencent closed at 402.71 HKD, down 9.79% over five sessions, and Alibaba's Hong Kong line at 105.30 HKD, down 11.88%, while KWEB fell 9.04% and FXI 6.80% over the same span; ASHR, the onshore CSI 300 proxy, rose 0.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters tied the rout to fresh fears of a regulatory crackdown [[n0171]], and Bloomberg reported Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth [[n0196]]. Primary-market appetite has faded too: Reuters reported Shein shelving its US IPO plan again on uncertain markets [[n1259]], and WSJ reported a US block-trading investigation hitting Morgan Stanley's plans to expand in China [[n0225]]. The yuan is the counterpoint, with China Daily arguing it will remain an investor safe haven [[n0218]].
New / Most Important

The war has sharpened the Taiwan question for portfolios. Reuters reported Beijing insisting Taiwan is 'not Ukraine' as the island raised its alert level [[n1320]], and separately Taiwan warning of Chinese aircraft in its air defence zone [[n1371]]. TSMC said it will comply with export-control rules on Russia [[n0653]], aligning Taiwan's leading chipmaker with Western sanctions. Foreign industrial capital is still committing to the mainland: Reuters, citing sources, reported Tesla planning a new Shanghai plant to more than double its China capacity [[n1913]].
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer onshore exposure such as ASHR, at 36.62 USD, over offshore internet such as KWEB, at 34.10 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: a two-sessions growth target and fiscal package that confirms the easing bias [[n0212]]. What changes the call: Western moves toward secondary sanctions on Chinese banks that facilitate Russian trade, or a default chain spreading from private developers to state-linked ones. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and the Shanghai Composite is stable, yet Tencent fell 9.79% in five sessions and private developers keep defaulting, so the easing has not reached the assets global investors actually own.

geo.label: BOJ patient, imported inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Japan imports the energy shock with a central bank still anchored at zero. The Nikkei 225 closed at 26,476.50 index points, up 1.95% on Friday but down 2.78% over five sessions and 1.98% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported consumer inflation in the capital perking up, with the Ukraine crisis set to add pressure [[n1048]], and The Japan Times reported the country bracing for even higher inflation [[n1463]]. Mixed: imported inflation squeezes real incomes faster than it changes policy, although Reuters noted a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1435]].
Activity & Currency

Momentum was fading before the war. CNBC reported February factory growth falling to a five-month low [[n1437]], after a GDP rebound that, per The Guardian Nigeria News, came before the Omicron wave hit [[n1433]]. With the BOJ pinned near zero while the Fed prepares to hike, the rate gap should keep the yen soft, turning dearer oil into a larger domestic cost; The Japan Times framed the war as a threat to the world's economic recovery [[n1462]]. Friday's equity rebound was led by the chip-equipment complex: Tokyo Electron rose 5.79% to 56,600.00 JPY, Advantest 7.71% to 9,220.00 JPY and SoftBank Group 5.56% to 5,069.00 JPY, while Toyota, at 2,104.00 JPY, is down 5.29% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Regional security remains a second risk premium after DW reported North Korea firing a ballistic missile [[n1417]].
Playbook ✓

Action: keep Japan at neutral through EWJ, at 63.55 USD and up 1.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), tilted toward exporters with pricing power and semiconductor equipment rather than energy-importing domestic names. Trigger: a BOJ signal that tolerates higher yields would favour Japanese banks and weigh on the weak-yen exporter trade. What changes the call: a further leg up in oil that pushes Tokyo-style price gains into wages, as The Japan Times' analysis of the war's economic consequences warns [[n1472]].

geo.label: RBA patient, commodity cushion
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is cushioned by commodities and constrained by cost-of-living politics. The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 6,997.80 index points, up 0.10% on Friday, down 3.10% over five sessions and up 0.14% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), after ABC reported a $74b one-day wipe-out followed by a rebound [[n0061]]. The RBA's line, per WSJ, is that it will not follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0025]]. Mixed: terms of trade improve, but households pay for the energy shock.
Demand & Financing

The AFR reported the last CPI spike at 3.5 per cent [[n0004]], yet ABC reported wages recording their worst result in seven years [[n0073]], which is the RBA's reason to wait. The labour market keeps tightening, as ABC's analysis of the falling unemployment rate shows [[n0087]], and financing costs are edging up at the margin, with ANZ lifting rates on some lending and savings accounts [[n0060]]. ABC warned the invasion drives up energy costs Australians will not escape [[n0081]]. Iron ore is the swing factor: The Australian reported China threatening an iron ore single market [[n0037]], and BHP closed at 39.79 AUD, down 6.82% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Playbook ✓

Action: favour resources outside the China iron-ore channel, such as Lynas, which rose 6.93% to 9.57 AUD on Friday, over the major banks, with CBA at 93.88 AUD and down 3.96% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger: an RBA shift away from patience if wages break higher. What changes the call: Chinese purchasing controls that cap iron ore, which would hit BHP and Fortescue, at 18.60 AUD, harder than domestic rate risk.

geo.label: NBP tightening on the frontline
parts: Macro Stance

Poland enters the week as NATO's frontline economy with inflation already at its highest of this century, per SII's reading of the January data [[n1537]]. Forsal.pl reported GUS putting January inflation at 9.2% [[n1536]], and Rzeczpospolita reported the RPP lifting rates to their highest in almost nine years [[n1531]]. Rzeczpospolita summarised the invasion's consequences as higher inflation and a weaker zloty [[n1666]], the worst mix for a central bank still catching up. The labour market is turning at the margin: Obserwator Gospodarczy reported unemployment rising for the first time in almost a year [[n1625]]. The structural support has been labour supply; INNPoland argued that without Ukrainians Poland's high GDP growth would be a dream [[n1621]], and war is now reshaping that pool. Bearish on duration and the currency, selective on equities.
Markets

Friday brought what Bankier called a historic rebound on the GPW, with banks coming to the rescue of the WIG20 [[n1694]], a day after a war-panic crash [[n1646]]. The Beta ETF WIG20TR closed at 33.93 PLN, up 7.71% on Friday but down 8.30% over five sessions and 9.81% over 20; PKO Bank Polski rose 13.27% to 40.72 PLN, Bank Pekao 17.14% to 118.60 PLN and mBank 12.81% to 389.20 PLN, yet mBank is still down 14.16% over five sessions, and the dollar-based EPOL closed at 18.45 USD, down 10.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The currency is the weak point: Forbes listed the zloty among the biggest losers of the war's outbreak [[n1729]], and Rzeczpospolita said it was the cheapest in months [[n1681]]. Business Insider Polska reported Poles withdrawing more cash, as at the start of the pandemic [[n1653]], while the NBP said its cash reserves are sufficient [[n1702]].
Fiscal & Politics

Security is now a fiscal line item. Bankier reported the government adopting the draft homeland-defence act and asked whether NBP profit will finance the armed forces [[n1590]], on top of pandemic spending that Rzeczpospolita said reached a record [[n1583]], and the World Bank's Poland public finance review [[n1485]] frames the trade-offs. Tax politics remain messy: Money.pl reported more than a hundred thousand Poles losing money because Polski Ład did not account for them [[n1747]], after Biznes Wprost reported dismissals at the finance ministry over the reform [[n1548]]. The anti-inflation shield is under strain at the pump, with Fakt warning of fuel at 6 zł and asking whether the government shield has stopped working [[n1749]], while TVN24 reported UOKiK will police fuel prices as Orlen cuts ties with stations that inflated them [[n1724]]. naTemat reported the PiS government demanding 'crushing' sanctions on Russia [[n1741]].
Corporate & Sectors

The corporate map splits on Ukraine exposure and commodity leverage. Rzeczpospolita reported Orlen introducing refuelling limits [[n1712]], Bankier reported it terminating contracts while imposing limits [[n1688]] and later that it had increased deliveries to the east where fuel ran short [[n1744]]; wnp.pl reported Russian crude is less than half of its refinery runs [[n1672]]. Orlen rose 10.96% to 69.86 PLN on Friday. LPP, which closed its Ukrainian stores and moved its Kyiv office to Lviv according to Wiadomości Handlowe [[n1665]], closed at 9,590.00 PLN, down 36.07% over five sessions, and Allegro, which Strefa Inwestorów said posted record fourth-quarter revenue but disappointing profitability [[n1687]], closed at 27.51 PLN, down 15.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Bankier reported CEO Francois Nuyts stepping down [[n1640]], and PKO BP's chief said the bank had prepared for every scenario at Kredobank in Ukraine [[n1656]]. KGHM rose 9.34% to 155.70 PLN and JSW 9.80% to 41.80 PLN; Wyborcza reported KGHM and Orlen pursuing small modular reactors [[n1734]].
Geopolitics & Security

The security premium is being met with physical reinforcement. Notes From Poland reported the UK sending an advanced air-defence system [[n1492]], GOV.UK announced UK forces arriving on NATO's eastern flank [[n1507]], and Onet reported the Polish army raising combat readiness [[n1673]]. Public opinion has shifted, with a Rzeczpospolita poll finding 71.1% of Poles think Russia could attack Poland [[n1667]], and Moscow has retaliated in the air, banning flights from Bulgaria, Poland and the Czech Republic, per Al Jazeera [[n1506]]. Al Jazeera reported tens of thousands fleeing to Poland [[n1509]], and Radio-Canada reported officials pledging help to all Ukrainians fleeing the war [[n1497]], a humanitarian commitment with fiscal and housing costs. Energy routing is the other front: Reuters reported Yamal-Europe flows running east [[n1480]], raising the strategic value of Baltic Pipe, which WysokieNapiecie examined [[n1547]].
New / Most Important

The weekend validated Warsaw's hard line: CBC reported a widening group of countries moving to block Russian access to SWIFT [[n1416]], and POLITICO reported the EU agreeing €500M in arms and aid for Ukraine's military in a 'watershed' move [[n1511]]. That makes Poland the logistics hub for Western support and a plausible target for Russian counter-measures. For the economy, Bankier's analysis that immigrants will first seek shelter before entering the labour market [[n1726]] implies a near-term cost to public finances ahead of any labour-supply dividend, while banks waiving fees for Ukrainians, per Business Insider Polska [[n1746]], is a small but visible hit to fee income.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish duration and zloty-sensitive assets, and fade Friday's bank-led bounce rather than chase it; within equities prefer commodity exporters such as KGHM and JSW over discretionary names with Ukrainian store networks such as LPP. Trigger: a renewed slide in the WIG20TR tracker below Friday's 33.93 PLN close alongside further zloty weakness would confirm the risk premium is rebuilding. What changes the call: an RPP move large enough to stabilise the currency, or a negotiated ceasefire that reopens the road to Polish rebuilding exposure. ⚠ Divergence: domestic buyers stepped in hard on Friday, with PKO up 13.27% and Pekao up 17.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and the NBP is publicly calming fears of cash-machine queues [[n1698]], so local positioning may already be cleaner than the currency's weakness implies.
Narrative

Technology was the fulcrum of the week's reversal, and YCharts was already asking how long tech stocks take to recover from a crash [[n1916]]. XLK closed at 154.35 USD, up 1.36% on Friday and 1.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), yet Barron's still described a bear-market scare in tech [[n0776]]. Balance sheets are the sector's defence, but it owns the most duration in a bear-flattening curve.
Reported

Nvidia's fourth-quarter release [[n0965]] remains the demand anchor, and Cisco raised its annual earnings forecast alongside $15 bln of buybacks [[n0962]]. Dell was the miss: Investor's Business Daily reported the stock tumbling after the company missed its earnings goal [[n0714]], and it fell 7.84% on Friday.
EPS Upside Watch

Apple is the upside case. Counterpoint reported Apple capturing its highest-ever smartphone share in the fourth quarter of a record ~$450 billion revenue year [[n1052]], and AAPL closed at 164.85 USD, up 3.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Cybersecurity is trading like defence. Palo Alto Networks closed at 569.75 USD, up 14.15% over five sessions, as Fox News warned Russian cyberattacks could come to the US [[n1403]]. Treat security software as a war hedge rather than as generic growth.
Narrative

Communication services is where sanctions policy meets platform economics. XLC closed at 68.53 USD, down 2.52% over 20 sessions, and Meta Platforms (FB) at 210.48 USD, down 28.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported Meta barring Russian state media from running ads [[n0753]] and Google blocking RT and other Russian channels from earning ad dollars [[n0815]]: compliance now has a revenue cost.
Reported

Roblox suffered its worst post-earnings drop, per Bloomberg [[n0969]]; Nexstar reported fourth-quarter net revenue of $1.25 billion [[n1010]]; and The Hollywood Reporter's studio profit report had Disney diving while Sony soared [[n1061]].
EPS Upside Watch

Meta's Reels push is the swing factor for FB. Reuters reported the global launch of its 'fastest growing' format [[n0998]], and Ad Age reported new creator ad features aimed at TikTok [[n1009]]. Upside requires Reels monetisation to close the gap with feed advertising before engagement shifts further.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Content moderation has become a geopolitical liability as well as a brand risk. Reuters' focus on Spotify's Joe Rogan saga spotlighted podcast moderation challenges [[n1850]]; SPOT closed at 151.91 USD, down 11.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Narrative

Financials rallied on Friday, with XLF up 3.22% to 39.10 USD and KRE up 4.60% to 73.84 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), but the weekend shifted the debate to sanctions plumbing. Kharon reported Sberbank landing on a rare US Treasury list [[n0772]], and the Los Angeles Times asked how American financial institutions will deal with Russia sanctions [[n0745]].
Reported

Canadian banks are the template: Reuters reported CIBC and National Bank beating estimates on lending and markets units [[n1075]], while RBC's profit rise came with a mortgage-slowdown flag [[n0114]]. Rocket Companies reported lower earnings but issued a special dividend [[n0115]].
EPS Upside Watch

The 2Y's 37 bps rise over 20 observations lifts asset yields, but the 21 bps compression in 10Y-2Y caps margins (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25); Kansas City Fed research asking whether margins at small and large banks respond differently to rates [[n2127]] is the right lens; asset-sensitive regionals benefit most.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Regulation, not credit, is the brokers' near-term risk. The Financial Times reported Morgan Stanley disclosing twin probes into big stock transactions [[n0608]], and Reuters reported an SEC investigation of Goldman Sachs over employee communications [[n0783]]. MS closed at 94.55 USD, down 6.52% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Narrative

Energy prices supply risk, but not fully. Brent closed at 97.93 USD/bbl and WTI at 91.59 USD/bbl, down 1.16% and 1.31% on Friday after Reuters reported oil topping $105 on the invasion [[n1927]]; Brent is still up 9.61% over 20 sessions and XLE up 4.51% at 68.88 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Time explained why sanctions are not targeting oil and gas [[n1400]], hence Friday's dip.
Reported

CNBC reported BP offloading its nearly 20% stake in Rosneft [[n0836]] after WSJ reported UK government pressure [[n0699]]. ExxonMobil agreed to sell its Nigerian shallow-water affiliate [[n1078]], and Reuters reported its workforce falling by 9,000 in 2021 amid cost cuts [[n0445]].
EPS Upside Watch

Chevron said it is monitoring Russia and can adjust crude supply [[n0551]]; CVX closed at 140.38 USD, up 5.07% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). US majors keep operating leverage to price; the debate is how much windfall boards return.
⚡ Breaking Convention

US gas tells a different story: Henry Hub closed at 4.47 USD/MMBtu, down 28.65% over 20 sessions, while TTF rose 26.04% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The transatlantic gap is a call option on US export capacity rather than on domestic prices.
Narrative

Defence has moved from hedge to budget line. POLITICO described Germany's historic shift to ramp up defence spending [[n1230]], and ITA closed at 107.63 USD, up 8.92% over 20 sessions, with Northrop Grumman up 9.54% and Raytheon Technologies (RTX) up 9.90% to 98.12 USD, while XLI rose only 0.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Reported

BAE Systems published full-year results [[n0527]] and said, per Reuters, that the invasion will sharpen the focus on defence [[n0539]]. Deere's price hikes powered an earnings beat [[n0979]], yet DE fell 8.82% over five sessions to 346.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Lockheed Martin rose 5.33% over five sessions to 409.49 USD and General Dynamics 6.33% to 227.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25); GovCon Wire reported a $108M Electric Boat maintenance award for General Dynamics [[n0734]]. European budget increases should feed US primes' export books with a lag.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Aerospace supply chains are the hidden war exposure. Bloomberg reported jet-engine makers looking for titanium outside Russia [[n0588]], and Reuters reported Safran boosting titanium stocks [[n0645]]. Boeing fell 5.67% over five sessions to 201.48 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and Reuters reported airlines tackling widening Russia risks [[n0696]].
Narrative

Consumer discretionary is most exposed to the energy tax on households. XLY closed at 176.19 USD, down 2.72% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), and ABC7 reported pump prices rising as President Biden promised to soften the blow [[n1366]]. Falling real incomes hit big-ticket and home categories first.
Reported

Home Depot beat estimates and sees sales growth, per CNBC [[n1001]], but Reuters flagged its margin warning [[n1002]]; HD fell 8.99% over five sessions to 316.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). TJX missed on Omicron store closures [[n0501]], and Foot Locker's 2022 forecast was hit by Nike's shift [[n0730]].
EPS Upside Watch

Carvana is the idiosyncratic upside: TechCrunch reported its $2.2B purchase of the Adesa US auction business [[n0547]], and CVNA jumped 21.04% to 152.57 USD on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Lowe's struck an optimistic tone on home-improvement demand despite rising rates [[n1032]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla's discount is governance as much as demand. WSJ reported an SEC probe into trading by Elon Musk and his brother after the CEO's share sales [[n0569]], and TSLA fell 7.59% over five sessions to 809.87 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Narrative

Staples took Friday's defensive bid: XLP rose 3.22% to 75.91 USD, Procter & Gamble 4.27% and Coca-Cola 3.87% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The offset is input costs; Food Dive reported food commodity prices soaring as Russia invaded [[n1941]], and wheat closed at 843.00 US cents/bu, down 8.96% on Friday but up 8.49% over 20 sessions.
Reported

Reuters reported Coca-Cola HBC's profits rising as it readied Russia contingencies [[n0340]], then the bottler shutting its Ukraine plant [[n0544]]; Nestle temporarily closed Ukrainian factories and warehouses [[n0610]], and Food Business News reported Danone volume dipping as supply-chain issues persist [[n0435]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power is the screen. CNN reported Burger King's largest franchisee cutting its chicken nugget count as prices surge [[n2106]], while Costco closed at 517.49 USD, up 7.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), the membership model's advantage in an inflation squeeze.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Shrinkflation is becoming a consumer-visible story, as The New York Times' question of what paper towels should cost shows [[n1100]]. Brands that cut pack sizes protect margins today but risk share loss to private label later.
Narrative

Health care is the cleanest defensive: XLV closed at 130.95 USD, up 3.06% on Friday and 2.41% over 20 sessions, with Eli Lilly up 4.10% over five sessions to 250.85 USD and AbbVie up 9.98% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Demand is non-discretionary and largely insensitive to energy prices.
Reported

WSJ reported Moderna beating profit estimates on COVID-19 vaccine sales [[n0602]], and CNBC reported the company expecting at least $19 billion in vaccine sales in 2022 [[n0604]]; MRNA still fell 3.14% to 151.33 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
EPS Upside Watch

Approvals are the upside lever: Fierce Pharma reported EMA expanding nods for Bristol Myers, Eli Lilly and Novartis drugs [[n1076]]. Novo Nordisk's US line closed at 102.75 USD, up 7.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Antitrust and drug pricing are the risks inside the defensive. Reuters reported the US suing to block UnitedHealth's $8 bln deal for Change Healthcare [[n0663]], and KFF found prices rising faster than inflation for half of all Medicare-covered drugs in 2020 [[n2173]].
Narrative

Materials price the supply shock directly. XLB rose 3.65% to 84.34 USD on Friday, aluminium closed at 3,406.00 USD/t, up 10.22% over 20 sessions, and Alcoa is up 34.15% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trade Data Monitor noted that Ukraine is more than a breadbasket, being a key iron ore and metals supplier [[n0039]].
Reported

Reuters reported MP Materials posting higher profit as rare-earth prices surged [[n0595]], and MP closed at 46.85 USD, up 12.62% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Newmont reported 2021 mineral reserves of 93 million gold ounces [[n0613]].
EPS Upside Watch

Fertiliser is the earnings lever: Bloomberg reported shortages linked to Russia-Ukraine tension may hit the US growing season [[n0452]]. Mosaic rose 9.22% on Friday and 25.42% over 20 sessions, Nutrien 17.20% and CF Industries 16.26% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Corporate restructuring continues despite the shock: Chemical & Engineering News reported Celanese buying DuPont's engineering polymer and elastomer businesses for $11 billion [[n0549]]. Vale expects the conflict to affect nickel and pellet prices [[n0704]].
Narrative

Real estate bounced as long yields stalled: XLRE rose 2.18% over five sessions to 45.86 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) while the 10Y held at 1.97% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25). The sector benefits from inflation-linked rents but loses if the Fed keeps lifting the front end.
Reported

Barron's reported Opendoor tanking after earnings [[n0126]], down 23.13% to 8.44 USD on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25); in Australia, the AFR reported inflation's silver lining helping Charter Hall Retail upgrade earnings [[n1030]].
EPS Upside Watch

Housing demand is cooling: the Guam Daily Post carried a report of new-home sales declining for the first time in three months [[n2115]], and National Mortgage Professional reported a Fed governor predicting sluggish home sales [[n2063]]. Upside sits with landlords that can reprice leases faster than financing costs rise.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Private capital keeps buying what public markets discount. Business Wire reported SmartStop Self Storage REIT acquiring a $280 million portfolio [[n0648]], and Blackstone Real Estate launched an affordable housing company [[n0543]].
Narrative

Utilities are a bond proxy with an energy-security kicker, and Friday showed the defensive bid. XLU rose 3.10% to 67.58 USD on Friday and 1.87% over five sessions, NextEra Energy is up 6.41% over 20 sessions and Southern Company down 4.40% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Reported

ABC13 reported CenterPoint Energy customers frustrated with a spike in natural gas prices [[n1964]], a reminder that pass-through invites customer and regulatory pushback; The Business Journals reported Duke Energy planning to combine operations at its two Carolinas utilities [[n0440]].
EPS Upside Watch

Merchant generators carry the upside: Enverus examined how ERCOT's ORDC changes are affecting market volatility [[n0108]], and Vistra closed at 21.90 USD, up 1.91% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Nuclear is being re-rated as security. URA rose 18.10% over 20 sessions and Cameco 23.83% to 22.81 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), as The New York Times reported climate fears moving to the back burner while fuel costs soar [[n1187]].
Narrative

European autos face supply, demand and sanctions shocks at once. The STOXX autos tracker closed at 59.18 EUR, up 3.68% on Friday but down 3.41% over five sessions; BMW fell 7.72% and Renault 15.91% over five sessions, while Volkswagen preference shares rose 2.90% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The market is discriminating sharply within the sector.
Reported

Reuters reported Stellantis' strong first year with cost challenges looming [[n0500]], and The Detroit News put its first-year profit at $15 billion [[n0497]]; Reuters reported scarcity and software set to power Mercedes-Benz through 2022 [[n0646]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen's Porsche listing is the re-rating catalyst: Reuters reported a framework deal with its top shareholder [[n0673]], and the Luxembourg Times reported VW keeping the IPO on the table amid volatility [[n0788]]. Mercedes-Benz Group is up 3.13% over 20 sessions at 72.06 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The binding constraint is parts, not demand. Yahoo Finance UK reported BMW suspending Mini production at Oxford due to the chip shortage [[n0419]], and The Statesman reported the war set to worsen that shortage [[n1965]].
Narrative

Semiconductors are holding up better than the war narrative suggests. SOXX closed at 477.06 USD, up 6.85% over 20 sessions, with Nvidia up 10.08% and AMD up 17.99%, while TSMC's ADR fell 7.12% over five sessions to 111.23 USD and ASML's US line rose 2.57% to 667.12 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Reported

Nvidia's fourth-quarter results, summarised in AlphaStreet's snapshot [[n0975]], underpin NVDA's 20-session outperformance; the Taipei Times reported UMC investing US$5bn in a Singapore plant [[n1092]].
EPS Upside Watch

TSMC's R&D chief told IEEE Spectrum there is light at the end of the chip shortage [[n1955]], and the EIU reported chip makers increasing investment for 2022 [[n1908]]. Equipment demand is the cleaner upside than pricing, which Tokyo Electron's 5.79% Friday gain reflects (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Valuation has already compressed: Barron's listed 15 chip stocks that keep getting cheaper [[n0526]], and Yahoo Finance reported AMD now worth more than Intel [[n0407]]. Share-takers, not incumbents, are being paid.

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance and cost discipline beat headline beats
parts: Rewarded

Block (SQ) was the clearest reward: the stock rose 26.14% to 119.82 USD on Friday and 15.19% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), after Payments Dive reported management defending higher marketing spending [[n1073]] and ABC reported Block soaring on the ASX as well [[n0061]]. Carvana rose 21.04% after Reuters reported its deal to buy KAR Global's US vehicle auction business for over $2 bln [[n0709]], and Barron's reported Stellantis soaring on a strong debut annual profit [[n0496]].
Punished

Opendoor fell 23.13% after results that Barron's argued left the real-estate firm 'misunderstood' [[n0126]], and Dell fell 7.84% after missing its earnings goal [[n0714]]. CNBC reported Coinbase posting a big revenue beat but expecting first-quarter trading volume to fall [[n0554]]; COIN lost 7.86% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Newsweek reported Moderna's $12 billion 2021 profit [[n0606]], yet the shares fell 3.14%, and The Guardian reported Rolls-Royce losing £1.5bn of share value after its chief executive said he would quit [[n0628]].
Pattern

The market is paying for forward evidence and punishing caution on volumes, margins or leadership. Block and Carvana were rewarded for strategic moves that extend their platforms; Coinbase, Moderna and Home Depot were punished despite beats because the outlook implied slower volumes, a vaccine peak or, in Home Depot's case, the margin warning Reuters flagged [[n1002]]. With the 2Y up 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25), a beat on trailing numbers is worth less than a credible path for the next four quarters, and long-duration stories need cash-flow proof sooner.
Attention into EPS

The next prints will be judged on three disclosures. Russia exposure comes first, as UniCredit's statement that its Russian arm is self-funded and well covered [[n0670]] and Societe Generale's assurance that Rosbank operates normally [[n0649]] show. Input-cost pass-through comes second, which Reuters reported Coles flagging [[n0028]]. Chip supply is third, with Reuters reporting Ford halting F-150 output in Kansas City [[n1080]].
Playbook

Own post-earnings winners only where the outlook, not the beat, drove the move; Block holding above its 105.64 USD late-January close is the template (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Fade beats that arrive with volume or margin warnings. What changes the call: if sanctions disclosures reveal larger losses at European banks, punishment will widen from single names to whole sectors and the reward for good guidance will shrink.

underowned.title: US LNG and gas-export infrastructure
parts: Attention Gap

Henry Hub closed at 4.47 USD/MMBtu, down 28.65% over 20 sessions, while Dutch TTF closed at 94.42 EUR/MWh, up 26.04% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). US gas is priced as a domestic weather trade even as The Economist asks whether LNG could plug the gap if Russian supply to Europe were cut off [[n1501]].
Exposure & Risk

Exposure runs through US liquefaction, shipping and the integrated majors' LNG books; Shell closed at 2,000.50 GBp, up 5.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The EIA reported three countries supplied almost 70% of Europe's LNG in 2021 [[n1170]]. Risk: liquefaction capacity is fixed in the short run, and a ceasefire would compress the spread quickly.
Trigger to Watch
The Washington Post reported the EU will unveil a strategy to break free from Russian gas [[n1351]]; long-term offtake contracts signed under it would turn the spread into contracted cash flow.

underowned.title: Cyber defence as national-security spend
parts: Attention Gap

Defence primes absorbed the war bid, but the cyber front is less crowded. CrowdStrike closed at 181.75 USD and Cloudflare at 109.27 USD, up 7.01% and 5.26% over five sessions, while Zscaler fell 15.77% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), so the group is still priced as volatile software rather than as security infrastructure.
Exposure & Risk

Data Center Knowledge reported Cloudflare buying Area 1 Security to fight phishing [[n0552]], and CrowdStrike's research on access brokers [[n1786]] maps the market for stolen network entry. Risk: these are long-duration growth stocks exposed to the same bear flattening that hit software.
Trigger to Watch

A state-linked attack on Western infrastructure. Gazeta Prawna reported Poland's prime minister raising the cyber alert level [[n1553]], and Niebezpiecznik published guidance on the war and cybersecurity in Poland [[n1683]].

underowned.title: Solar and distributed power as energy security
parts: Attention Gap

The New York Times reported climate fears moving to the back burner as fuel costs soar [[n1187]], yet Enphase Energy rose 28.14%, SolarEdge 32.46% and Bloom Energy 53.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The market is re-labelling domestic generation as supply security.
Exposure & Risk

Apollo launched a sustainable investing platform and sees more than $100 billion of energy-transition deployment by 2030 [[n1906]], and Offshore Wind reported TenneT tendering 2 GW of German offshore grid connections [[n1201]]. Risk: higher rates raise project-finance costs, and module supply chains remain concentrated.
Trigger to Watch
Budget follow-through on Germany's energy-security pivot, which the BBC described as a dramatic U-turn [[n1232]]; procurement for storage and grid would broaden the trade beyond panels.

underowned.title: Japanese semiconductor equipment
parts: Attention Gap

Tokyo Electron rose 5.79% to 56,600.00 JPY and Advantest 7.71% to 9,220.00 JPY on Friday, yet Tokyo Electron is up only 0.34% over 20 sessions and Advantest down 2.64%, against AMD's 17.99% gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Exposure & Risk

The EIU reported chip makers increasing investment for 2022 amid the shortage [[n1908]], and TechCrunch reported Bosch investing $296M to produce semiconductors [[n1867]]. Risk: a yen spike in a risk-off episode, tighter export controls on China-bound tools, and a cyclical pause in chipmakers' spending that would hit equipment orders first.
Trigger to Watch

New foundry capex. The Taipei Times reported UMC investing US$5bn in a Singapore plant [[n1092]]; further announcements of that kind feed equipment order books directly and would narrow the gap with US chip leaders.

crypto.title: Bitcoin fails the safe-haven test, then finds a sanctions narrative
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin's last completed day closed at 37,709.79 USD, down 3.57% on the day, 1.51% over five days and 13.98% over 20; ether closed at 2,621.80 USD, down 5.73% on the day and 16.57% over 20, and Solana at 85.52 USD, down 27.13% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-27). Yahoo Finance UK said the invasion blew safe-haven claims to bits [[n0922]], and CNBC argued the case for bitcoin as 'digital gold' is falling apart [[n0915]], even though bitcoin and ether climbed with the late-week broader rebound, per CNBC [[n0703]]. Gold, at 1,887.60 USD/oz and up 5.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), is the hedge that worked.
New / Most Important

The BBC reported millions in bitcoin pouring into Ukraine from donors [[n0948]], giving crypto a wartime utility story. The SWIFT measures, which CNA explained as a possible path to sanction Russia [[n1404]], raise the question of whether sanctioned entities will try crypto rails, a risk that would invite tighter enforcement rather than adoption. In the US, SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce told Barron's she is amazed a bitcoin ETF has not been approved [[n0949]], while Bloomberg reported Coinbase's revenue beat came with a caution on trading volume [[n0553]]. Bloomberg also reported one of the biggest crypto traders tapping DeFi loans for funding [[n0934]], a reminder that leverage in the system is migrating, not disappearing.
Playbook

Action: size crypto as a high-beta risk asset, not a hedge, and keep it small while the VIX sits at 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Trigger to add: a daily close back above 43,840.29 USD, bitcoin's level of 2022-02-07 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-27), would show it decoupling from equity risk. What changes the call: evidence that sanctions enforcement targets exchanges, or regulatory movement on the spot ETF Peirce described; the former is a sell signal, the latter a durable bid.

flows.title: Liquidity is tightening into a war shock
parts: Global Liquidity

The liquidity regime was turning before the invasion. TD Economics argued quantitative tightening will slow deposit growth and put modest upward pressure on yields [[n0113]], and Capital Economics said 'we need to talk about QT' [[n1147]]. The IIF reported emerging markets driving global debt to a record $303 trillion [[n1249]], which leaves the system sensitive to a dollar-funding squeeze. The war adds a second channel: barring some Russian banks from SWIFT, as The New York Times reported [[n1412]], removes counterparties from the plumbing and encourages intermediaries to hoard liquidity. Primary markets are the first casualty: Riviera reported deteriorating conditions forcing Fred Olsen Windcarrier to put its IPO on hold [[n1237]], and the Luxembourg Times reported VW keeping the Porsche IPO on the table amid volatility [[n0788]]. When the issuance window shuts, sponsors waiting to exit stay locked in and fresh equity supply dries up, which supports index levels in the short run but starves the pipeline of growth listings.
Rates & Dollar

The dollar's haven move was brief. Reuters reported it jumping to a near two-year high on invasion day [[n1210]] before investors regained risk appetite and the dollar and oil pared gains [[n2160]]; the DXY closed Friday at 96.62 index points, up 0.86% over five sessions and down 0.66% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Treasuries left a positively sloped curve with the 2Y at 1.55% and the 10Y at 1.97%, bear-flattening over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25). Duration has paid nobody: TLT is down 4.34% and IEF 1.29% over 20 sessions, while SHY has lost only 0.60% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), so the front end remains the least costly place to hold liquidity. China Daily's argument that the yuan will remain an investor safe haven [[n0218]] is the policy-managed exception. The emerging-market transmission is visible: EMB closed at 100.17 USD, down 4.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), Reuters reported Indian shares and the rupee plunging as Russia attacked [[n1357]], and Forbes ranked the zloty among the biggest losers of the war's outbreak [[n1729]].
Credit Check

US credit is bending, not breaking. HYG closed at 83.61 USD, up 1.01% over five sessions and down 0.98% over 20, while LQD is down 3.20% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), a duration loss rather than a default signal. Stress is concentrated: Reuters reported Russian bonds hammered as the rouble plummeted [[n1332]], The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over its bond default [[n0170]], and Retail Banker International described Western sanctions slamming bank stocks [[n1975]]. China's property credit remains a slow-burn source of defaults, with CNBC reporting Moody's downgrading Shimao [[n0205]], and Brown Brothers Harriman is pitching structured credit as a toolbox against uncertain rate environments [[n1261]]. Issuers with access are locking in funding, as RBC Capital Markets' note on Ford's record $2.5 billion green bond shows [[n1250]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Flow evidence points to hard assets and defence. Reuters reported big inflows into gold ETFs on geopolitical concern [[n1255]], and the Financial Times reported ETF investors piling into Russian equities and defence stocks before the invasion [[n0904]], a bottom-fishing trade that the invasion-day crash in Russian stocks, which CNN put at 33% [[n0638]], promptly punished. Investopedia described investors fleeing stocks for refuge in gold and bonds [[n0675]]. Corporate buybacks remain the steadiest buyer: Time reported Buffett taking a 'mildly attractive' path with $27 billion of repurchases [[n0827]]. Among managers, Forbes reported Li Lu bulking up Meta and Bank of America while shedding Pinduoduo [[n0748]], Investor's Business Daily highlighted three shrewd moves by top Fidelity managers in a bad market [[n0780]], and CNBC asked readers who panic-sold during the week's volatility when to get back in [[n1969]], a measure of how fast sentiment swung.
Portfolio Implication

Price action overstates the all-clear. Friday's rally left the VIX at 27.59 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) and a front end still repricing the Fed, and the weekend added SWIFT exclusions and German rearmament. Keep liquidity buffers higher than usual, prefer short-dated Treasuries to credit duration, hold gold and energy as the hedges that have worked, and treat the IPO and high-yield windows as shut until volatility settles. The signal to re-risk is two-sided: tighter HYG pricing and a weaker DXY together would show the funding channel easing, while a stronger dollar with falling EMB would show it seizing.

anticipatory.title: Ukraine–Russia talks: Friday priced the good outcome
parts: What Is Priced

Reuters reported a Ukrainian official saying Kyiv is ready for talks with Russia on neutral status [[n1397]], and PBS reported China calling for talks [[n1350]]. The S&P 500's 2.24% gain and the VIX's 9.00% drop to 27.59 index points on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25) price a negotiation path more than they price the weekend's escalation.
Conditional Expression

If talks produce a ceasefire framework, the cleanest expression is long European cyclicals against defence: the DAX is still down 4.91% over 20 sessions while Rheinmetall is up 15.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). If talks fail or stall, reverse the pair and add energy, with Brent at 97.93 USD/bbl and the risk premium still building.
Risk

Talks can coexist with escalation. UN News reported Russia blocking Security Council action on Ukraine [[n1408]], and VOA reported Belarus holding a constitutional vote as the crisis rages [[n1414]]. A headline-driven pair can be stopped out twice in one session, so size it smaller than conviction suggests.

anticipatory.title: Fed March lift-off: 25 bps priced, 50 bps the tail
parts: What Is Priced

The 2Y at 1.55%, up 37 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-25), prices lift-off. Al Jazeera reported a Fed official leaving the door open to a half-point hike in March [[n2058]], while Xinhua reported a Fed official signalling that a March hike is on track despite the Ukraine crisis [[n2180]].
Conditional Expression

If the Fed confirms 25 bps with war-related caution, the 2Y should stall near 1.55% and the curve steepen from +42 bps, favouring asset-sensitive regional banks such as KRE at 73.84 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). If it signals 50 bps, flatteners and the dollar win, and leveraged long-duration tech such as TQQQ, up 4.74% on Friday, is the short.
Risk

CNBC reported in January that the Fed points to a March hike [[n2121]], so lift-off itself is near-certain; the risk is the path, which the January readout, per Reuters, did not tie to any particular pace [[n2130]]. A dovish surprise on the path would hurt the flattener more than the dollar.

anticipatory.title: ECB taper path under an energy shock
parts: What Is Priced

ECB policymakers told Reuters not to go back on quicker taper plans [[n1224]], and Reuters' projection has the deposit rate rising to -0.25% by year-end [[n1131]]. Bloomberg's report of Brevan Howard having one of its best-ever trading days on an ECB bet [[n1186]] shows how violently euro-area rates move when guidance shifts.
Conditional Expression

If the ECB holds its taper plan through the war, European banks gain on margin hopes despite Russia exposure: Societe Generale is down 13.37% over 20 sessions and has the most to recover. If it pauses, FEZ, at 43.19 USD and down 2.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), loses bank support but gains duration relief, favouring quality growth over financials.
Risk

Energy inflation at 27%, per Eurostat [[n1220]], makes a pause hard to justify and a hike hard to deliver into a supply shock. The ECB can keep both camps disappointed, so express the view through relative trades rather than outright euro-area beta.

anticipatory.title: China's two sessions: growth target and easing
parts: What Is Priced

Onshore equities are pricing policy support: ASHR rose 1.50% on Friday to 36.62 USD while KWEB is down 9.04% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). Reuters reported slowing inflation leaving room for easing [[n0149]], and Bloomberg described the People's Bank seizing the moment for stimulus [[n0134]].
Conditional Expression

If the growth target and fiscal quota are ambitious, add to onshore exposure and to infrastructure-linked commodity names, with aluminium at 3,406.00 USD/t (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). If they are cautious, the onshore premium over offshore internet narrows and the relative trade should be cut.
Risk

Policy can ease while regulators keep tightening on platforms. Bloomberg's report of Alibaba planning for a new normal of low growth [[n0196]] says the offshore discount is about earnings power, not liquidity, so a stimulus package need not rescue KWEB. A Western move toward secondary sanctions would hit both legs.

catalysts.title: Block (SQ) — outlook-led re-rating
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Block rose 26.14% to 119.82 USD on Friday and 13.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), with Payments Dive reporting management defending higher marketing spending [[n1073]]. CNBC's account of Square's growth from scrappy hardware start-up to payments powerhouse [[n0584]] frames the thesis: spending to deepen the ecosystem is being rewarded while rates rise.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is holding the gap above 105.64 USD, the late-January close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The risk is that high-beta fintech re-rates lower as the 2Y climbs, which would close the gap regardless of execution.
Trade Expression
Buy pullbacks toward the gap rather than chasing; pair against PayPal, at 110.94 USD and down 29.83% over 20 sessions, to isolate execution from sector beta.

catalysts.title: Rheinmetall (RHM.DE) — Germany's rearmament proxy
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

DW reported Germany committing €100 billion to defence spending [[n1228]], and Reuters reported European defence stocks rising as Russia invaded [[n0565]]. Rheinmetall closed at 107.05 EUR, up 7.00% on Friday, 11.00% over five sessions and 15.06% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The question now is how quickly budget becomes orders.
Price Hurdle & Risk
The stock has already moved far above its 93.04 EUR late-January close. Risk: procurement takes years, and a ceasefire would trigger profit-taking long before budgets are disbursed.
Trade Expression

Hold core exposure and add on pullbacks rather than chasing the gap; Joint Forces News' report of Rheinmetall presenting an HX 8×8 excavator with CSM [[n0768]] shows the HX truck platform's reach beyond combat orders.

catalysts.title: BP (BP.L) — the Rosneft exit
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reported BP offloading its nearly 20% stake in Rosneft [[n0836]] after WSJ reported pressure from the UK government [[n0699]]. BP closed at 378.50 GBp, up 3.60% on Friday but down 1.80% over 20 sessions, while Shell is up 5.56% over 20 at 2,000.50 GBp (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25). The exit removes a sanctions overhang at the cost of whatever the stake contributed to earnings.
Price Hurdle & Risk
The first test is whether the market treats the decision as a write-down or as a de-risking. Risk: the size of the loss and the lost cash flow are not yet quantified.
Trade Expression
Prefer Shell over BP until BP quantifies the Rosneft hit, then reassess; a BP close above 385.45 GBp, its late-January level, would signal the market has looked through it.

catalysts.title: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B) — buybacks as the deal
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported Buffett lamenting a lack of good investments even as Berkshire profit set a record [[n0807]], and Forbes Middle East put 2021 net profit at $89.8B [[n0837]]. CNBC reported the annual letter calling Apple one of the 'Four Giants' driving Berkshire's value [[n0828]]. BRK-B closed at 319.24 USD, up 3.56% on Friday and 3.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Price Hurdle & Risk

The risk is opportunity cost: without large acquisitions, returns rest heavily on buybacks. Business Insider reported Buffett blasting fake earnings [[n0826]], a reminder the stock is a cash-flow compounder, not a momentum vehicle.
Trade Expression
Own as quality ballast against long-duration growth; add if the price holds above 307.67 USD, its late-January close.

catalysts.title: Moderna (MRNA) — beat versus durability
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

WSJ reported Moderna beating profit estimates on COVID-19 vaccine sales [[n0602]], and CNBC reported the company expecting at least $19 billion in 2022 vaccine sales [[n0604]], while Fierce Pharma put its forecast at $22B [[n0605]]. The shares still fell 3.14% to 151.33 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25), because the debate is durability, not the quarter.
Price Hurdle & Risk

BioPharma Dive reported Moderna advancing a 'bivalent' booster [[n0603]], but Fierce Biotech reported Merck cutting ties to its early KRAS vaccine [[n0601]]. Risk: pipeline setbacks matter more than booster volume once pandemic demand fades.
Trade Expression
Stay neutral; a close above 148.62 USD, the late-January level, keeps the range intact, while a break below it would signal the market is discounting the post-pandemic revenue cliff.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA) — the new normal of low growth
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Borneo Bulletin reported Alibaba's slowest revenue growth since going public as competition bites [[n0805]], and Modern Retail reported the company betting on international growth as regulatory pressure grows [[n0534]]. The US ADR closed at 107.94 USD, down 13.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-25).
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is reclaiming 111.79 USD, the late-January close. Risk to the bearish view: an aggressive stimulus package would lift all China assets, and The Japan Times' report of banks being told to report exposure to Ant [[n0161]] could also end in a resolution that removes an overhang.
Trade Expression
Underweight versus onshore exposure such as ASHR; cover if the stock reclaims its late-January level with improving volumes.
